stem: In the primary survey of a severely injured child after a high-speed motor vehicle collision, which trauma series X-ray is least likely to help identify the source of haemorrhage?
explanation: Among the standard trauma series films, chest and pelvic X-rays can identify major sources of bleeding (thoracic and pelvic), and long bone imaging can identify bleeding from femoral or other long bone fractures. A cervical spine X-ray is used to assess spinal injury, not haemorrhage.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: The question asks which trauma series film is least useful for finding bleeding. C-spine imaging is for spinal assessment rather than haemorrhage localisation.

optionExplanations.A: May reveal thoracic injuries such as haemothorax that can cause haemorrhage.
optionExplanations.B: May identify pelvic fractures, an important source of major bleeding.
optionExplanations.C: Assesses spinal injury and is unlikely to identify the source of haemorrhage.
optionExplanations.D: May identify long bone fractures, which can contribute to blood loss.

The following text applies to the questions at positions 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21

Clinical Scenario 2 - Penny

Teaching/Learning points:

Cardiovascular assessment

Physiological differences in children with shock

Approach to resuscitation / fluids

Blood on the floor… and four more (chest, abdomen, pelvis and long bone).

The emergency department receives an advanced warning from the ambulance service of a high-speed motor vehicle collision on the motorway nearby. At least three cars are involved and there have been a number of fatalities. Fire rescue services and a pre-hospital medical retrieval team are on the scene as a number of casualties are trapped and require extrication.

Your unit will be receiving

Penny,

a three year old female, who was found at the roadside some five metres from the main scene. It is thought she was ejected from one of the vehicles involved, in which two adult occupants died at the scene. She has been intubated at the scene due to reduced conscious level.

Vital signs are:

Respiratory rate 25bpm (ventilated)

Saturations 98% in 50% oxygen

Heart rate 120bpm

Blood Pressure 95/40.

She has multiple abrasions over her face and torso. ETA is 15 minutes...

The following nine questions refer to Penny’s clinical scenario.
